examples.solution_text: The net has six equal squares. The four squares in a row fold around the sides, and the other two close the top and bottom. It makes a cube.
The net has two matching triangles and three rectangles. The triangles become the two ends, and the rectangles fold around them. It makes a triangular prism.
The square becomes the base. The four triangles fold up and meet at one point. It makes a square-based pyramid.
The net has four matching triangles. One becomes the base, and the other three fold up and meet at one point. It makes a triangular-based pyramid.
The two matching circles become the ends. The rectangle wraps around them to make the curved surface. It makes a cylinder.

coverage.summary: Added five worked examples covering four distinct assessed methods, including both pyramid base types. Questions and solutions are separate editable fields; solution prose inherits the renderer's blue. Diagrams use unshaded black outlines and reveal no solid names. No equation gutters are needed. Assessments were classified only and remain unchanged; independent example review and final visual capture remain pending.

examples.derivation: Six unit squares form a valid cube net: four consecutive squares wrap around the sides, and the squares attached above and below the third square close opposite ends. This adapts the cube recognition task in image7.

Each rectangle measures 2 by 3 coordinate units. Both triangular ends have base 2 and height sqrt(3), giving three sides of length 2. The matching edges fit, and attaching the triangles to opposite ends of different rectangles produces a valid triangular prism net. This follows image8 b and image9.

The base is a square of side 2. Each attached triangle has base 2, altitude 2 and equal sides sqrt(5). These faces meet consistently at an apex above the square centre, producing a square-based pyramid. This adapts image8 d.

The outer equilateral triangle has side 4. Its midpoint connections partition it into four equilateral triangles of side 2. The three outer triangles fold around the central triangle to form a triangular-based pyramid, matching image8 c.

Both circles have radius 0.7. Their circumference is 1.4π, equal to the rectangle's width; its height is 2.5. The rectangle therefore wraps around the two matching circular ends to form a cylinder. This adapts image13 f; circumference is a reviewer consistency check, not additional student content.
